deadline: Saturday (earlier than usual due to sprint format)
central_unknown: McLaren's reliability and competitiveness remain the biggest wildcard — they won here last season with a 1-2 but have been inconsistent all year with battery and mechanical issues. Whether Ferrari can keep pace on Silverstone's long straights (where they've historically suffered clipping) or fall back behind Red Bull and McLaren is the other key question.

budget_tiers.core: Antonelli (captain), Hamilton or Verstappen as Tier A, Mercedes constructor

budget_tiers.fills: Lawson, Lindblad or Bortoleto, Colapinto or Hadjar

captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Kimi Antonelli
captains.reason: Consensus pick across all channels. Championship leader with 40-point gap, looked 'far and away the best boost option' in Austria FP2 despite a DNF in the race. Betting odds have him neck-and-neck with Russell at the top for Silverstone. All analysts agree he's the clear captain choice.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: Lewis Hamilton
captains.reason: Record 9 wins and 15 podiums at Silverstone, 12 straight podiums before last season's P4. Only Tier A driver on track for a max price rise. FanAmp and ZachGP both highlight his home race pedigree, though Ferrari's form at Silverstone is a concern with long straights and potential clipping issues.

buy.name: Nico Hulkenberg
buy.note: Price floor — cannot lose budget. 82% ownership in global top 500. Finished on podium at Silverstone last season (P3 from P19). Consensus must-own across all channels. Once Barcelona DNF drops off rolling average, he becomes a strong budget builder.

buy.name: Isack Hadjar
buy.note: Strong recent form, solidified P8 in championship. On track for a good price rise needing only ~9 points at Silverstone. Multiple analysts recommend Gasly-to-Hadjar swap as a key move this week. Better long-term hold than Gasly due to rolling average.

buy.name: Arvid Lindblad
buy.note: Preferred budget option over Bortoleto per F1FantasyPolePosition. Needs only -2 points for min price rise at Silverstone. 28 points over last two races (14 per race avg). Racing Bulls car looks competitive in midfield. Strong overtaking and position gain stats.

consider.name: Franco Colapinto
consider.note: Dropped in Austria but not as badly as feared. Needs 8 points for min price rise, 17 for max. Sprint weekend helps. Some analysts moving away from him to fund other upgrades.

consider.name: Liam Lawson
consider.note: Averaging 13 points per non-DNF race. Good hold but not exciting — described as a 'luxury transfer' to move away from. Needs 7 points for min price rise at Silverstone. VCARB looked like top-of-midfield fifth fastest team.

consider.name: Gabriel Bortoleto
consider.note: Consistent 5-7 point floor but lacks double-digit upside. No double-digit score since first race. Lindblad preferred by most analysts if choosing between the two.

consider.name: Max Verstappen
consider.note: Runner-up in Austria moved him level with Hamilton in betting odds. Red Bull showing resurgence. Noted that Silverstone might be 'a completely different track' with new regs. Needs 11 points for min price rise — tough but possible on sprint weekend.

avoid: Valtteri Bottas — three consecutive mechanical DNFs with Cadillac, massive price drops (down 1.5M from purchase). Even at 3.0M, must see him finish a race before considering.
Sergio Perez — Cadillac reliability risk at 6.2M is not worth it when Lindblad and Bortoleto are cheaper and safer. Best teams in fantasy have zero Cadillac or Aston Martin exposure.
Cadillac (constructor) — both cars DNF'd in Austria with mechanical failures. Unreliable and uncompetitive.
Aston Martin (constructor) — described as 'still wank' by ZachGP, no competitive upside.
Esteban Ocon — specifically called out as disappointing differential option, avoid.

chips.name: Triple Captain (3x)
chips.reason: ReinFantasy strongly advocates using 3x chip at Silverstone. Sprint weekend means more scoring opportunities, Antonelli is a near-consensus captain lock, and upcoming non-sprint weekends offer fewer points. The combination of sprint points + strong captain pick makes this one of the best remaining windows for the chip.

chips.name: Wildcard
chips.reason: FanAmp discusses chip options but the consensus leans toward saving the wildcard. Budget positions are still evolving and the summer break after Belgium could be a better restructuring point.

chips.name: Limitless
chips.reason: No channel recommends using Limitless this weekend. Better saved for a weekend with clearer form differentials or a non-sprint race where squad construction is more constrained.

watch_items: FP1 is the ONLY practice session before sprint qualifying — decisions must be made quickly with very limited data.
McLaren battery reliability: Norris may or may not have received the new Mercedes battery fix. If McLaren sort reliability, they become a top constructor pick.

Ferrari clipping on Silverstone's long straights — Leclerc finished P14 in the last two British GPs and lost positions in four straight races here. Watch FP1 pace closely before committing to Ferrari constructor.

Mercedes constructor vs McLaren constructor decision: George Russell had car issues in Austria FP2 while McLaren looked strong. If Russell shows pace in FP1, Mercedes is safer; if not, McLaren is tempting but risky.
Weather: Currently forecasted 26°C, cloudy, 3% rain chance on Sunday. Ralfulo on X says virtually no rain expected — removes wet weather variable.
Pirelli compounds are C1/C2/C3 (hardest available) — could produce 2-3 stop races. Track has averaged 3.75 DNFs per race over last four seasons.
Red Bull upgrades not clicking for Hadjar in Austria (radio complaints about car feel) — monitor if resolved at Silverstone before committing.
Gasly to Hadjar transfer is a key move many analysts are planning — if you haven't done it, this may be the week.
Hulkenberg's Barcelona -50 DNF score drops off rolling average soon, making him a strong budget builder in coming weeks.
arc: Silverstone is one of the last sprint weekends before the summer break, making it a critical scoring and budget-building opportunity. The decisions made here — particularly around constructor choice (Mercedes vs McLaren vs Ferrari) and whether to deploy the 3x captain chip — will shape lineups heading into the Belgian GP at Spa, which is a very long track where budget builders like Lindblad and Bortoleto may struggle to hit price rise thresholds. After Belgium, the summer break offers a natural reset point. Players who nail Silverstone's sprint weekend with the right captain and chip deployment will enter the second half of the season with a significant leaderboard and budget advantage. The Gasly-to-Hadjar transition and Bottas-to-Hulkenberg cleanup are moves that need to happen now to stop falling behind the top 500 meta.
